arxiv-2104-14216.title: A near-infrared interferometric survey of debris-disk stars Thanks: Based on observations made with ESO Telescopes at the La Silla Paranal Observatory under program IDs 093.C-0712 and 094.C-0325.
arxiv-2104-14216.creator: O. Absil ,, L. Marion, S. Ertel, D. Defrère, G. M. Kennedy, A. Romagnolo, J.-B. Le Bouquin, V. Christiaens, J. Milli, A. Bonsor, J. Olofsson, K. Y. L. Su, J.-C. Augereau
arxiv-2104-14216.description: Abstract Context. Hot exozodiacal dust has been shown to be present in the innermost regions of an increasing number of main sequence stars over the past fifteen years. The origin of hot exozodiacal dust and its connection with outer dust reservoirs remains however unclear. Aims.

arxiv-2307-12404.title: Crystal structures and high-temperature superconductivity in molybdenum-hydrogen binary system under high pressure
arxiv-2307-12404.creator: Aiqin Yang, Xiangru Tao, Yundi Quan, Peng Zhang
arxiv-2307-12404.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Aiqin Yang, Xiangru Tao, Yundi Quan, Peng Zhang. Motivated by advances in hydrogen-rich superconductors in the past decades, we conducted variable-composition structural searches in Mo-H binary system at high pressure. A new composition-pressure phase diagram of thermodynamically stable structures has been derived.

arxiv-2311-11875.title: Neutrino Oscillations in Finite Time Path Out-of-Equilibrium Thermal Field Theory
arxiv-2311-11875.creator: Ivan Dadić, Dubravko Klabučar *
arxiv-2311-11875.description: Abstract We demonstrate that the Finite-Time-Path Field Theory is an adequate tool for calculating neutrino oscillations. We apply this theory using a mass-mixing Lagrangian which involves the correct Dirac spin and chirality structure and a Pontecorvo–Maki–Nakagawa–Sakata (PMNS)-like mixing matrix. The model is exactly solvable.

arxiv-2405-18511.title: Feasibility and benefits of joint learning from MRI databases with different brain diseases and modalities for segmentation
arxiv-2405-18511.creator: Wentian Xu \midljointauthortext Contributed equally 1, Matthew Moffat \midlotherjointauthor 1, Thalia Seale 1, Ziyun Liang 1, Felix Wagner 1, Daniel Whitehouse 2, David Menon 2, Virginia Newcombe 2, Natalie Voets 3, Abhirup Banerjee 1, Konstantinos Kamnitsas 1
arxiv-2405-18511.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Wentian Xu \midljointauthortext Contributed equally 1, Matthew Moffat \midlotherjointauthor 1, Thalia Seale 1, Ziyun Liang 1, Felix Wagner 1, Daniel Whitehouse 2, David Menon 2, Virginia Newcombe 2, Natalie Voets 3, Abhirup Banerjee 1, Konstantinos Kamnitsas 1. Models for segmentation of brain lesions in multi-modal MRI are commonly trained for a specific pathology using a single database with a predefined set of MRI modalities, determined by a protocol for the specific disease.

arxiv-2406-03707.title: What Should Embeddings Embed? Autoregressive Models Represent Latent Generating Distributions
arxiv-2406-03707.creator: Liyi Zhang zhang.liyi@princeton.edu, Michael Y. Li michaelyli@stanford.edu, R. Thomas McCoy tom.mccoy@yale.edu, Theodore R. Sumers ted@anthropic.com, Jian-Qiao Zhu jz5204@princeton.edu, Thomas L. Griffiths tomg@princeton.edu
arxiv-2406-03707.description: Abstract Autoregressive language models have demonstrated a remarkable ability to extract latent structure from text. The embeddings from large language models have been shown to capture aspects of the syntax and semantics of language. But what should embeddings represent? We show that the embeddings from autoregressive models correspond to predictive sufficient statistics.

arxiv-2409-12333.title: Scale-specific auxiliary multi-task contrastive learning for deep liver vessel segmentation
arxiv-2409-12333.creator: A. Sadikine, B. Badic, J.-P. Tasu, V. Noblet, P. Ballet, D. Visvikis, P.-H. Conze
arxiv-2409-12333.description: Abstract Extracting hepatic vessels from abdominal images is of high interest for clinicians since it allows to divide the liver into functionally-independent Couinaud segments. In this respect, an automated liver blood vessel extraction is widely summoned. Despite the significant growth in performance of semantic segmentation methodologies, preserving the complex multi-scale geometry of main vessels and ramifications remains a major challenge.

arxiv-2501-14132.title: Time-Dependent Queuing Model for Traffic Congestion Using Mt/D/1/K: Simulation and Policy Insights
arxiv-2501-14132.creator: Jyoutir Raj
arxiv-2501-14132.description: Abstract This study proposes a generalised macroscopic traffic simulation using a M t / D / 1 / K M_{t}/D/1/K queue to model congestion, using the Enniskillen to Belfast route as a case study. Empirical traffic data from Google’s Directions API is used to calibrate the model, thus explaining peak commute times which we model using queue length.

arxiv-2502-06172.title: PLATTER : A Page-Level Handwritten Text Recognition System for Indic Scripts
arxiv-2502-06172.creator: Badri Vishal Kasuba, Dhruv Kudale, Venkatapathy Subramanian, Parag Chaudhuri, Ganesh Ramakrishnan
arxiv-2502-06172.description: Abstract In recent years, the field of Handwritten Text Recognition ( HTR ) has seen the emergence of various new models, each claiming to perform competitively better than the other in specific scenarios. However, making a fair comparison of these models is challenging due to inconsistent choices and diversity in test sets.

arxiv-2511-02077.title: Beyond Static Cutoffs: One-Shot Dynamic Thresholding for Diffusion Language Models
arxiv-2511-02077.creator: Jucheng Shen, Yeonju Ro
arxiv-2511-02077.description: Abstract Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLM) are becoming competitive with their autoregressive counterparts but commonly decode with fixed steps and sequential unmasking. To accelerate decoding, recent works like Fast-dLLM enables parallel decoding via a static global confidence threshold, yet we observe strong block/step-wise confidence fluctuations and, within a dataset, near-identical confidence trajectories across inputs indicated by cosine similarity.

pmc-10793367.title: Bilateral Necrotizing Scleritis with Scleral Melt associated with Herpes Simplex Infection: A Case Report
pmc-10793367.creator: Arti Singh, Ashutosh Maharana, Srishti Nagarajan, Shubhi Sachan
pmc-10793367.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Objective (Aim): The article is a case report of a very rare case of bilateral herpes simplex virus infection associated with bilateral necrotizing scleritis with scleral melt in an elderly north Indian female of lower middle socioeconomic status. Methods: A 65-year-old female presented to our clinic with a wide variety of presentations ranging initially from neurotropic corneal ulcer to necrotizing scleritis with scleral melt for 2 years. The patient records were evaluated and computed.

pmc-11599331.title: Comparative analysis of airborne fungal spore distribution in urban and rural environments of Slovakia
pmc-11599331.creator: Matúš Žilka, Michal Hrabovský, Jozef Dušička, Eva Zahradníková, Dominika Gahurová, Jana Ščevková
pmc-11599331.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Monitoring airborne fungal spores is crucial for public health and plant production since they belong to important aeroallergens and phytopathogens. Due to different land use, their concentration can differ significantly between urban and rural areas. We monitored their spectrum and quantity on two geographically close sites with a different degree of urbanisation: Bratislava City and Kaplna Village in Slovakia, located 38 km apart.

pmc-12978449.title: Towards equitable and immersive outdoor orienteering: An artificial intelligence-driven multi-objective route planning framework with augmented sand cat swarm optimization
pmc-12978449.creator: Qingzhu Lun, Boya Li, Yuehui Zhou
pmc-12978449.description: Outdoor orienteering has emerged as a globally popular recreational activity and competitive sport, combining navigational challenges with physical endurance across diverse natural terrains. Despite its growing popularity, the design of optimal orienteering routes presents significant challenges for recreation planners, requiring careful consideration of both competitive fairness and participant engagement.

pmc-13109655.title: Differential associations between traumatic brain injury severity and four dementia phenotypes in military veterans
pmc-13109655.creator: Victoria C. Merritt, Elizabeth Valocchi, Francesca V. Lopez, Georgios Asimakopoulos, Alexandra L. Clark, Lay Kodama, Amy J. Jak, Lin Liu, Catherine Chanfreau‐Coffinier
pmc-13109655.description: INTRODUCTIONNational Veterans Affairs electronic health records were used to examine the association between traumatic brain injury (TBI) severity and four dementia phenotypes ranging from narrow (strict AD) to broad (all‐cause dementia).METHODSVeterans with TBI (n = 91,753) and a propensity score‐matched comparison group of veterans without TBI (n = 183,506) were included.

pmc-13261344.title: Fertility preservation in prepubertal boys: management and follow-up challenges
pmc-13261344.creator: Vittorio Ferrari, Federico Baronio, Marcello Lanari, Rod T Mitchell
pmc-13261344.description: Survival after childhood cancer and severe haematological disorders has improved substantially, shifting clinical attention towards long-term quality-of-life outcomes. Preservation of male reproductive potential represents a major challenge, particularly in boys exposed to gonadotoxic therapies before the onset of spermatogenesis. While sperm cryopreservation is an established fertility preservation strategy for postpubertal males, no clinically validated option currently exists for prepubertal boys.

pmc-13266756.creator: Mario Shuchleib Cukiert, Guillermo Roa Alvarez, Sergio Dib Fajer, Sergio Enrique Leal Osuna

pmc-13373951.title: Case Report: Successful topical simvastatin therapy in a 2-year-old girl with keratin 16-associated palmoplantar epidermal differentiation disorder
pmc-13373951.creator: Qingmei Zhong, Ying Zhang, Zhen Feng, Jinyan Zhang, Borui Chen
pmc-13373951.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Palmoplantar epidermal differentiation disorder associated with pachyonychia congenita is a rare autosomal dominant genodermatosis characterized by painful palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and nail dystrophy. Treatment options remain limited, particularly in young children, in whom systemic therapies carry safety concerns. Herein, we report a 2-year-old girl who presented with palmoplantar hyperkeratosis since 1 month of age, with progressive nail dystrophy involving all 20 nails.

pmc-13406666.title: Adaptive Digital Marketing: A Systematic Review of Bio-Inspired Reinforcement Learning, Multi-Agent Systems, and Agentic AI for Intelligent Optimisation
pmc-13406666.creator: Tek Narayan Adhikari, William Sayers, Shujun Zhang
pmc-13406666.description: Background: Digital marketing increasingly functions as a complex adaptive system characterised by non-stationary environments, strategic interaction, and multi-agent competition. Programmatic advertising exemplifies this complexity, where decisions must be made in real time under uncertainty. Under such conditions, traditional static optimisation methods often fail to deliver robust performance.

pmc-13542548.title: Research progress on agricultural water information sensing and applications in high-altitude cold regions
pmc-13542548.creator: Yang Yang, Yikai Xu, Libin Su, Yonggang Guo, Yongtao Yang
pmc-13542548.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Agricultural water management is essential for food security in high-altitude cold regions, such as the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, the Rocky Mountains, and the Alps. However, extreme environmental conditions—including low temperatures, intense radiation, and complex terrain—impede traditional hydrological monitoring. This narrative review systematically evaluates “space-air-ground” multi-source sensing technologies, summarizing recent advances in satellite remote sensing, low-altitude Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), and cold-resistant ground sensors to address these constraints.
